description:
We are XR developers and 3D artists with experience in previous NASA Space Apps Challenges, specializing in Unity, Blender, and Meta Quest SDKs.

We are developing Space BCE, an immersive VR simulator for Meta Quest 3S. Players will step into the role of a NASA chief engineer and evaluate how their engineering decisions impact mission success.
summary: We created an immersive virtual reality experience using Unity and NASA resources, where users become astronauts and participate in a space mission divided into four stages: spacecraft preparation, launch, lunar landing, and orbital docking. Through interactive controls and technical challenges, players make decisions that influence mission success. The experience brings space engineering closer to users, allowing them to explore, experiment, and learn from their decisions in a virtual environment. Space BCE combines simulation, technology, and interactive learning to inspire interest in space exploration and promote STEM education, contributing to SDG 4: Quality Education.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

Space BCE is an immersive virtual reality game designed to help users understand space mission operations and engineering decisions through interactive experiences.

Players assume the role of astronaut-engineers, preparing spacecraft, operating controls, solving technical problems, and experiencing the consequences of their decisions.

The project proposes three mission stages:

  • Stage 1 — Hangar Preparation: Players inspect spacecraft systems, identify technical failures, repair components, and complete pre-launch safety checks.
  • Stage 2 — Cockpit Ascent: Players experience a rocket launch, operate flight controls, manage acceleration, perform stage separation, and respond to simulated emergencies.
  • Stage 3 — Moon Landing: Players control a lunar descent, monitor altitude, operate propulsion controls, and attempt to land safely in a designated area.
  • Stage 4 — Orbital Docking: Players approach a space station in lunar orbit, align their spacecraft using navigation controls, perform docking maneuvers, transfer mission data, and complete spacecraft shutdown procedures.

The game also proposes a mission-planning system where players can select spacecraft configurations and consider factors such as mass, energy, fuel, and payload.

The gameplay follows five steps: Plan → Prepare → Operate → Evaluate → Retry.

Currently, the team is developing the rocket launch environment in Unity. Additional interactions, mission stages, and evaluation mechanics are planned for future development.

What benefits does it have? What is the intended impact of the project?

Space BCE aims to make space science and engineering more accessible through immersive, practical learning.

The project encourages problem-solving, technical decision-making, and interest in STEM education. Virtual reality allows users to explore spacecraft environments and practice simulated procedures without the costs or risks of real space operations.

Sustainable Development Goal 4 — Quality Education

Space BCE directly aligns with SDG 4, particularly Target 4.4, by promoting technical knowledge and engineering-related skills through interactive educational experiences.

Its intended impact is to complement traditional learning with an engaging environment where users can experiment, make mistakes, and improve their understanding of space missions.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project? 

  • Unity 6000.3.21f1: Main development engine for the space simulation.
  • Blender: 3D modeling and spacecraft asset preparation.
  • NASA Resources: Spacecraft models and engineering documentation used as technical references.
  • Meta Quest 3S: Target hardware for the virtual reality experience.

Addition:

The team used the Kanban methodology to make the distribution of work among each member more flexible and understandable according to their specialty.

We also established a process diagram to be able to know the sequence of tasks that each one needs from the other and reduce the times of non-parallel work.

Finally, a general architecture of the four game stages was designed to demonstrate the intended gameplay and mission progression.
